what_it_does: Diffusion models—the AI systems that generate images and videos by gradually refining random noise—demand a very different hardware recipe than other neural networks. This 22-nanometer accelerator is optimized for them using a technique called compute-in-memory, where math actually happens inside the memory chips instead of shuttling data back and forth. The key insights: diffusion uses wildly different amounts of data per layer, so the accelerator has smart memory partitioning that matches bandwidth allocation to actual layer demands. It includes specially tuned circuit blocks for attention operations on 3D volumes and video sequences. At 60.81 trillion operations per joule, it's among the most energy-efficient accelerators for generative AI, attacking the 59% energy overhead that typically goes into just moving data.
